implementerProof.how: The pod was replaced, so I rebuilt INFRA-589's stack (harness d6916b3676ca plus the restart-scenario patch, own LOADTEST_ROOT and ports) and built Dispatch from the workspace (head), from git archive c3d09eec (base) and from a248dad3 (round 2). Round 3's three proofs hold on that surface: rolling update with a successor running beside the old process (all attempts sent once, each recipient stores each comment once), the unanswered session:<id> suppression (a person's reply in a thread the mentioned session rooted reaches it once at a 600 ms listener; round 2 twice), and the Stage 3 audit's fallback (base: fallback line, rig flagged, clean passes; head: log route). Earlier rounds' proofs re-checked at this head: stream boundaries, reconnects, relay/hub reads, agent-stream budget, kill recovery, restart replay bytes.

failures.criterion: Mention delivery runs off the request path and is not lost (INFRA-514: no event lost); a comment reaches each session it is for at least as surely as before.
failures.evidence: With Dispatch's ENVOY_URL through 'loadgen proxy -rtt 30s' (a listener that answers nothing; the mention send's own recheck then fails after the client's 5 s window), a person comments mentioning session:ses-x. routecopy.sh (LGA-6 routed to session:ses-x): head 12aada04 writes suppress_route=true, the attempt fails, and ses-x's NATS subject stores 0 copies; base c3d09eec writes suppress_route=false, the attempt fails, and ses-x stores 1 copy (the route copy, id dispatch-13001). authorcopy.sh (a reply in a thread ses-x rooted): head writes suppressed_authors=[ses-x], 0 copies; base suppressed_authors=[], 1 copy (the author-route copy). With a live listener every case gets 1 copy on both builds. Creation suppresses the route or author copy because the mention will deliver, and the mention's send then fails. The route case dates from round 1 (string-equal suppression, the architect's option A); the author case is new in round 3 (e587ca77). Red test: TestASilentListenerStillLeavesTheSessionOneCopyOfTheComment in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/comment_delivery_silent_listener_test.go (commit 'test(dispatch): a silent listener still leaves the routed or root-author session one copy of a mentioned comment'); `cd packages/envoy && GOWORK=off DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<postgres url> go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run TestASilentListenerStillLeavesTheSessionOneCopyOfTheComment -count=1` fails both subtests at head ('no event of comment ... was published to notifications.agent.s1, and its mention failed: s1 got no copy of the comment'); at a248dad3 the reply subtest passes and the route subtest fails.

proof.criterion: Mention delivery is not lost across a SIGKILL or a rolling update, and each recipient gets each comment once.
proof.surface: The load-test stack, listener at 2 s round trip; stack.sh restart-dispatch with SIGKILL 0.3 s into the drain; a second envoy-dispatch on the same database as the successor; each recipient's NATS subject read with $JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET
proof.observed: SIGKILL: 24 of 24 attempts sent, sends starting 60-70 s after the kill and done by 100 s, each of ses-a/b/c stores c1..c8 once, in order. Rolling: 4 comments committing during the old process's drain (12 'mention sender has stopped' lines); the successor sends all 30 attempts, each recipient stores the 10 comments once, the one in flight at the SIGTERM last, about 125 s after it. Two live processes, 45 comments to one recipient (143 s backlog): 45 stored once, in order, none duplicate.
proof.negativeControl: Round 1's head 153513a3 (round 1): after the same SIGKILL, c2's attempts stayed pending and no recipient got c2.

observations: Kill recovery is slower than round 2: an attempt queued but never started now waits a claim lease before any pass takes it (sends begin 60-70 s after a SIGKILL); the implementer records this trade-off.
